calibration.verdict: REFUSED_PAIRS_PASS: 1 of the 115 pairs the board's own prices refused are accepted by this rule -- they are listed with their numbers

caveats: two gates, both on PRICE only: a pair that passes is one the prices cannot tell apart for a year minus event days -- it is not a statement about the holdings
the line is calibrated on the board's own SAME-NAME families (r1804); applying it across names is an extrapolation, and the calibration block is republished each run
distribution policy is invisible here: two same-basket tickers that pay different dividends drift in price and are refused by gate 2 (a false refusal, not a risk)
the money line is the dearest-vs-cheapest premium INSIDE an accepted family on a 100000 CNY ticket; it is the price of picking the wrong name, not a return
one session of premiums: the family membership rests on a year of closes, the money on one day's board
the screen drops tickers that did not trade every day of the window (70 here); they are counted, never filled with zeros

sentence: On this board's own prices, 867 pairs cannot be told apart for a year and do not walk apart; 464 of them are written under two different names. Those pairs gather into 12 families that span more than one name, and in 2 of them the dearest member carries more than 0.50 pp of extra premium over the cheapest -- on a 100,000 CNY ticket that is 1,311 CNY for nothing but picking the wrong name. A further 1344 pairs move together day to day but walk apart over the year (a swap is a bet), and 166,279 do not move together at all.

year_line_decision.because: no pair the board's own prices refused drifts less than 0.4 pp/yr, so the labelled set cannot place the line between 1.0 and there; the line is priced by what being wrong costs -- a swap made inside a 1.0 pp/yr band loses at most that band, while the 351 extra pairs a 3.0 pp line recovers each carry up to 3 pp/yr of drift
year_line_decision.what_it_costs: recall: 468 of the 870 same-name pairs the prices accepted are refused
